pr_title: net: ip: Fix packet flood in 802.15.4 promiscuous mode
pr_body:
When 802.15.4 driver working in promiscuous mode and neighbor
cache enabled, we should drop our own packets, received back after
retransmission

Fixes #26919

Signed-off-by: Eug Krashtan <eug.krashtan@gmail.com>
pr_comments: Need to develop another way to fix this.

issue_context.title: ipv6: promiscuous mode: packet flood over 802.15.4 adapter
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

When 802.15.4 driver working in promiscuous mode and neighbor cache enabled, in some network configurations (more than 2 nodes placed in nearest locations) we observe packet flood generation as a result of unfiltered packet retransmission:

https://snipboard.io/GrqEWt.jpg

**To Reproduce**

Set "CONFIG_NET_PROMISCUOUS_MODE=y"
Place devices near each other, it was pretty hard to find the exact way how to reproduce this rare behavior.

**Expected behavior**

The device should ignore its own retransmitted packet.

**Impact**

Network speed degradation

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS:  Windows
 - Toolchain Zephyr SDK, GCC
 - Commit SHA ffd8e8aefcee4acff280e834ce55a8646d7cc195
comments:
Created PR to fix this bug 
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/26920
This bug was the result of dropping one part of the fragmented packet. I suppose after fixing https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/27010 this bug also disappears.

review_comments: @tbursztyka Agree. In general, we should always drop packets with our src as it has no sense to spend resources for packet handling.

I don't think this is the right approach. There's nothing wrong in sending a packet to our own IP address (promiscuous or not):
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/4783b7ebde9252ebdf863d35e7c7e26cfd2f4dd6/subsys/net/ip/net_core.c#L307
In this solution such packets will likely get filtered out.
@rlubos oh yes of course, if we have 2+ addresses. Completely overlooked that.
Probably we need some extra filtering in `ipv6_nbr.c` layer instead, @jukkar?
True. Will investigate this issue deeper
